positive.reasoning: Criterion A1 (traumatic event): MET — patient confirmed experiencing a distressing event that felt threatening and significantly impacted them. Criterion B1 (re-experiencing): MET — patient described overwhelming thoughts about the event and strong reactions to reminders. Criterion B2 (avoidance of thoughts): MET — patient reported a constant urge to push thoughts away and avoid reminders. Criterion B3 (avoidance of reminders): MET — patient stated they avoid certain places and conversations that remind them of the event. Criterion C1 (inability to recall details): MET — patient mentioned difficulty recalling specific details of the event. Criterion C2 (negative beliefs): MET — patient expressed a tendency to focus on negative thoughts about themselves and others. Criterion C3 (blame): MET — patient reported blaming themselves for not doing something differently. Criterion C4 (negative emotions): NOT MET — patient indicated negative feelings come and go rather than being constant. Criterion C5 (diminished interest): MET — patient stated they avoid activities that used to matter. Criterion C6 (detachment): MET — patient described feeling distant from others. Criterion C7 (inability to feel positive emotions): MET — patient reported difficulty feeling good. Criterion D1 (irritability): MET — patient acknowledged increased irritability. Criterion D2 (recklessness): MET — patient mentioned engaging in riskier behavior. Criterion D3 (hypervigilance): MET — patient reported being more alert and on edge. Criterion D4 (startle response): MET — patient noted being startled more easily. Criterion D5 (concentration difficulties): MET — patient described difficulty focusing. Criterion D6 (sleep disturbances): MET — patient reported more difficulty sleeping. Total: 14 of 20 criteria met (threshold ≥1 for each criterion). Duration: met (symptoms began after the event and have persisted for more than a month). Functional impairment: met (patient reported significant distress and interference with work and social interactions). Exclusions: not triggered (no substance use or medical conditions reported). Diagnosis: TRUE — full criteria met with significant functional impairment confirmed.
